transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Maya P (Redwood AE), Diego R (Redwood SE), Lena V (Redwood CSM), Jared C (MediCore CTO), Priya N (ML Lead), Samir K (SRE), Asha M (Compliance)

[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we thought we'd run through a very practical playbook today — bench, tune, and rollout for INT8 and FP8, plus how the Sandbox in the Optimize console makes that safe and repeatable.
[00:18] Jared Cole: yeah, sounds great. we care about throughput for chat assistants and also the hallucination risk — so quality matters.
[00:25] Diego Ramos: absolutely — i'll share my screen, quick note: sorry if a few things get munged in the auto-transcript, i know the mic on my laptop is meh.
[00:39] [screen share starts]
[00:42] Diego Ramos: ok, this is the Optimize sandbox. on the left you'll see qprofiles we already have — default-int8, fp8-accurate, hybrid-latency — these are templates that map to inference kernels, activation folding, and calibration datasets.
[01:05] Priya Nair: can you clarify calibration dataset? we normally calibrate on in-domain requests, right?
[01:11] Diego Ramos: yes, exactly. we recommend using 500-1k prompts representing production distribution. sandbox lets you upload that set, runs calibration sweeps, and produces a candidate INT8 profile with per-layer sensitivity scores.
[01:24] Priya Nair: per-layer sensitivity scores — we saw something like that in a paper but never in prod tooling. nice.
[01:30] Samir Khan: quick ops question — when you say sandbox, is traffic ever touching our VPC? we need to know egress rules and whether keys leave our network.
[01:39] Lena Volk: great question — for Private deployments we'd run the sandbox in your VPC; for Hosted sandbox we isolate data, use envelope encryption and our KMS integration; keys never land in plain text in logs.
[01:51] Asha Mehta: and for SOC 2 / audits, do you provide audit logs for calibration runs?
[01:57] Maya Patel: yes — all runs can be tied to an audit trail, run-id, and we capture the dataset hash. we'll add that to the security zip i'll send.
[02:06] Jared Cole: ok, show us some numbers — give a realistic latency hit or improvement when switching from fp16 -> INT8 and when using FP8.
[02:13] Diego Ramos: sure — caveat: model and sequence-length dependent. for a 32k-parameter-ish encoder-decoder style model used in our testbed: fp16 baseline median p95 token latency = 120ms; INT8 with tuned qprofile on same infra dropped median to ~90ms and p95 to ~140ms with a small quality delta. FP8 aggressive profile gave median ~80ms but p95 jittered more if KV cache wasn't warmed.
[02:44] Priya Nair: small quality delta — can you quantify? rouge/EM or human eval?
[02:49] Diego Ramos: in our internal eval set, INT8 had ~1 to 1.8% degradation on rouge-like metrics vs fp16; FP8 aggressive saw ~2.5-4% depending on prompt class. but for many assistant prompts, those deltas are imperceptible. that's why we recommend targeted evals — your clinical QA prompts might be sensitive.
[03:08] Priya Nair: good point — clinical fidelity tests are a must for us.
[03:12] Maya Patel: and the Optimize console ties eval results to the profile: you can see per-case regressions and set thresholds — if a profile fails the golden-set checks, the rollout can be blocked automatically.
[03:26] Diego Ramos: now demoing the benchmark flow — step 1: upload prompt corpus; step 2: select candidate models; step 3: choose qprofile templates (we do int8 calibrate, then fp8 sweep); step 4: run correctness and perf jobs. jobs show live traces, token-level latency, and cost delta.
[03:48] [00:03:48 — short screen scroll noises]
[03:55] Jared Cole: curious about KV cache interactions — you mentioned p95 jitter — is that because cache warming varies or because attention kernel differences?
[04:05] Diego Ramos: both. FP8 kernels sometimes change memory layout and cache prefetching behavior; that affects initial tokens. We recommend a warmup phase in the benchmark: run the prompt once per session type to populate KV and measure steady-state.
[04:20] Samir Khan: ops wise, what's the recommended batch size — we need to keep latency SLO at 200ms p95 for user-facing chat.
[04:28] Diego Ramos: for chat with small responses, single-request batching with continuous batching at the runtime layer is optimal; with dedicated instances you can bump batch size to 4-8 for throughput but watch p95. the console will show simulated p95 under your target qprofile and batch config.
[04:44] Priya Nair: are there automated fallback rules? if INT8 shows a regression on a particular prompt class, can it fallback to FP16 or FP8?
[04:52] Maya Patel: yes, Smart Routing + Rollouts. you can namespace by route and set automatic fallback to a pinned variant (e.g., fp16 or fp8-accurate) when regression thresholds spike or latency SLOs breach.
[05:03] [05:03 — inaudible chatter — someone coughs]
[05:10] Diego Ramos: jumping to the cost view — we show token-level cost delta. on our sample workload INT8 saved ~32% token compute cost vs fp16; FP8 saved ~44% but had more variability. the Optimize console suggests hybrid profiles — use INT8 for common assistant flows and FP8-accurate for long-form summarization routes.
[05:36] Jared Cole: hybrid profile — meaning per-route profile selection? or within a single request?
[05:42] Diego Ramos: per-route or per-model-variant. we also support sequence-length aware routing: short queries hit INT8-fast variant, longer queries go to fp8-accurate because precision matters.
[05:55] Priya Nair: could you show an example of how we might split routes? we have triage, summarization, and sensitive-clinical.
[06:02] Diego Ramos: sure — on the right nav we have 'Routes'. create route 'triage' -> attach model variant 'model-x-int8-fast', set p95 SLO 200ms; route 'summarize' -> 'model-x-fp8-accurate', SLO 400ms; route 'clinical' -> 'model-x-fp16' locked. then you can A/B test or gradual rollout.
[06:22] Maya Patel: note for procurement: Dedicated vs Hosted. If you need guaranteed p95 and private keys, Dedicated or Private deployment in your VPC is recommended. Hosted sandbox is great for initial tuning though.
[06:36] Asha Mehta: compliance asks — can the sandbox runs be done in our cloud account with your orchestration? we prefer that for any PHI-adjacent data.
[06:45] Lena Volk: yes, Private offers bring-your-cloud option; we can deploy the Optimize runtime and tooling inside your project, with RBAC and KMS hooked to your HSM.
[06:55] Jared Cole: what about model variants — do you support trimmed models or 4-bit quantization? we saw some vendors pushing 4-bit.
[07:03] Diego Ramos: we support a range: per-layer INT8, mixed bits, and FP8 when the backend supports it. 4-bit is experimental for larger models; it can give big speedups but higher risk of fidelity loss. we capture per-layer sensitivity to highlight layers where 4-bit is risky.
[07:21] Priya Nair: any gotchas on prompt engineering for quantized models? we saw some hallucinations with aggressive quant.
[07:27] Diego Ramos: yes — prompts that rely on long-context memorized tokens can be sensitive. the console's regression explorer will surface case-level diffs and token attribution highlighting where logits diverged during candidate runs.
[07:40] [07:40] Jared Cole: ok let's talk bench plan — what do you propose we run in the sandbox first week?
[07:46] Maya Patel: proposed plan: week 0: sandbox access + dataset upload; week 1: run calibration sweep (INT8) and FP8 baseline; week 2: focused eval on golden set + human QA for clinical prompts; week 3: reliability run (24–48h steady state) and cost projections.
[08:03] Priya Nair: how long does a calibration sweep take? we have 1k prompts and a couple model variants.
[08:09] Diego Ramos: depends on infra size. on a 4-GPU sandbox, calibration + correctness tests will usually finish in 3–6 hours. perf runs can be configured overnight for long tails.
[08:20] Samir Khan: can Redwood provide sample infra sizing recommendations? we need to provision Dedicated nodes if we go that path.
[08:26] Maya Patel: yes — we'll include a sizing worksheet in the sandbox invite that maps qprofile, concurrency, and SLOs to GPU counts and networking.
[08:35] [08:35] Jared Cole: question on tracing — do we get token-level traces that map to our APM? we want to stitch traces in Honeycomb/NewRelic.
[08:43] Diego Ramos: we emit structured traces and correlation ids; we can push to OTLP exporters or provide an export file. we'll also include token-level latency histograms per request id.
[08:55] Priya Nair: one more — model updates: if a new upstream model patch arrives, how do qprofiles survive? do we need to re-calibrate?
[09:03] Diego Ramos: small patch often ok, but we recommend a re-calibrate if weights change beyond a threshold. Optimize has a 'compatibility check' that computes a weight-shift score and flags the need to re-run calibration.
[09:16] Asha Mehta: for the audit trail, is the dataset hash immutable and can we export it for compliance?
[09:22] Lena Volk: yes, hash and run metadata are exportable; we also keep RBAC events tied to user identities.
[09:29] [09:29] Jared Cole: do you have any customers in health who've run similar workflows?
[09:33] Maya Patel: yes, a couple of EHR providers used the sandbox for med-summarization, one kept clinical routes on fp16 and moved triage to INT8 — reduced cost ~30% with no perf regression on clinical QA.
[09:45] Priya Nair: great. can we try an initial pilot with an emphasis on summarization and triage?
[09:50] Maya Patel: absolutely — we'll provision the sandbox and outline the bench script.
[09:54] [09:54] Diego Ramos: flipping to the console's regression explorer — here you can sort by delta in confidence, see token diffs, and mark false positives. for regulatory flows you can tag prompts as 'block on regression'.
[10:12] Priya Nair: can human QA be integrated in the loop? our clinicians prefer manual review before rollout.
[10:18] Diego Ramos: yes, the CSM flow includes a human review queue. we can export the flagged cases for review and re-run after fixes.
[10:27] Samir Khan: network policy question again — for private deployment, do agents talk outbound to Redwood control plane?
[10:34] Lena Volk: only to the control plane for metrics and licensing; we can also do an air-gapped option where exports are batched and uploaded via secure channel.
[10:43] [10:43] Jared Cole: ok last few items — pricing and contract length for Dedicated vs Private?
[10:48] Maya Patel: i'll send a pricing sheet — Dedicated is reserved capacity with commit tiers; Private is an enterprise license plus support. we'll include an ROI calc in the spreadsheet.
[10:58] Priya Nair: procedural — what does success look like for us after the sandbox?
[11:03] Maya Patel: success criteria: 1) a qprofile that meets golden-set thresholds (no more than X% regression on clinical set), 2) sustained p95 below 200ms for triage route under expected concurrency, 3) cost savings plan showing at least 20% reduction in token compute.
[11:19] Jared Cole: that sounds reasonable.
[11:22] [11:22] Maya Patel: ok, quick recap and next steps — we'll provision sandbox, send security artifacts, and Diego will run the initial INT8/FP8 sweep. Priya will upload the prompt set and Samir will share SRE requirements. we'll reconvene after benchmarks.
[11:34] Priya Nair: thanks everyone.
[11:36] Jared Cole: thanks, guys. good session.
[11:40] [end of recording]
